source.name: gbrain-install
source.note: Not a Harbor task source: the gbrain install trial reuses the frontier blocklist rules (scripts/egress/egress_blocklist.py) for its open-egress proxy (runner/trial/egress.ts).

egress.how: runner/trial/egress.ts startOpenEgress: every host and port is reachable except the patterns below (a "*" matches any characters); every connection, admitted or refused, is one line of the trial's egress log.

why.api.particle.ai: Particle's model API: every model call goes through the metering proxy, so a direct call from the container (a key the agent found, or gbrain configured with one) is refused and logged
why.openrouter.ai: OpenRouter's model API, for the same reason; the metering proxy is the only route to a model
why.*.openrouter.ai: OpenRouter subdomains, for the same reason
why.api.voyageai.com: Voyage embeddings: gbrain can embed with Voyage, and the keyless install must make no provider request at all; a direct call is refused and logged
why.gbrain.io: hosted gbrain: its setup needs a person to pick a plan in the browser, so the hosted route cannot finish without one; the agent sees it refused and the egress log records that it tried
why.*.gbrain.io: hosted gbrain subdomains, for the same reason
why.gbrainio.terminalwire.sh: the hosted gbrain installer (curl -sSL https://gbrainio.terminalwire.sh | bash), the first path INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md offers; refused for the same reason, and the attempt is logged as the hosted route
